The *Tissattheragāthā* (Thag 1.39) is a short Pali verse text preserved within the *Theragāthā* collection of the Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. The text records an inspired utterance attributed to the elder (thera) Tissa [SuttaCentral]. The poem has been translated into English by Bhikkhu Sujato, and SuttaCentral records a total of thirteen translations across eleven modern languages [SuttaCentral].

In terms of textual parallels and reuse, curated records identify passage-level correspondences within the Saṃyutta Nikāya—specifically the *Sattisutta* (SN 1.21) and the *Vāsudattasutta* (SN 2.16)—as well as within the *Theragāthā* itself, namely the adjacent *Vaḍḍhamānattheragāthā* (Thag 1.40) and the *Mahāmoggallānattheragāthā* (Thag 20.1) [SuttaCentral]. In paracanonical exegetical literature, the verse is cited in the *Peṭakopadesa* (Pe 2, Sāsanapaṭṭhānadutiyabhūmi) and the *Nettippakaraṇa* (Ne 37, Sāsanapaṭṭhāna) [SuttaCentral].
